correctness.rationale: The exact 27-term coefficient convolution reduces, after an invertible four-phase normalization, to M=104+4|S1|^2+8Re(D conjugate(S2)). An independently implemented exact Laurent-polynomial convolution verifies the identity from first principles. Newton identity 2S2=S1^2-(1+A^2+B^2+C^2) and triangle inequalities give M>=88. Saturation forces A,B,C real signs with exactly two negatives and D=1, proving precisely three orbits; all-one convolution bounds give M<=216 and force A=B=C=D=1 for equality. Continuity gives full interval; q-ary counts follow a free four-dimensional modulation action; finite grid orthogonality holds at orders >=3. Standalone checker passed exact symbolic and binary/quaternary computations, which are corroboration rather than a continuum proof.

value.rationale: The complete 2-by-2-by-2 Cartesian Fourier aperture is the smallest full three-coordinate instance. Its exact single-array fourth-moment energy is the canonical aperiodic autocorrelation sidelobe invariant, and the sharp ratio 8/3 is the corresponding merit factor. The global continuous-phase optimum has only three discrete quadratic-Boolean phase orbits, with no improvement over binary signs; the if-and-only-if even phase-alphabet threshold and exact q^4 counts give a meaningful structural obstruction relevant to polyphase array design. This is not a routine sum identity: it includes a sharp nonlinear inequality and complete equality classification. The exact optimum for odd alphabets and larger arrays is not asserted.
